independent.summary:
dropNearEmptyChunks is applied to chunkText() output, which includes the synthetic LEO-018 hours chunk appended at scraper.js:703-704. A typical terse footer hours chunk — content '[Source: …]
[H2] Hours

Monday - Saturday: 7 am - 2 pm' — has a chunkBody() of exactly 30 chars (the [Source] and [H2] Hours lines are discounted as the leading header block), under MIN_CHUNK_BODY=40, so it is dropped before embedding. That silently reverts the fix for the documented top Known Issue ('RAG misses what are your hours?') on exactly the dosiedough.com-shaped single-line hours table the module was written for; only sites with two or more paired hours lines keep the chunk. No test covers the hours chunk against the new filter.

The near-empty rule partially re-breaks LEO-083 for small thin-page groups. In a group chunk the leading header block is just '[Source: groupUrl]' and every other [Source:] line is discounted, so a group containing one card is measured as only its [H1] plus body: '[H1] Bob Lee' + 'bob@gbc.org' = 24 chars < 40, and the chunk is dropped — the staff member disappears from the KB. The test only exercises a two-card group (42+ chars), so the single-card/short-name boundary is untested even though multi-URL grouping exists precisely to stop thin staff pages from being lost. Compounded on rescrape: embedThinPageGroups still returns the groupUrl, so the previously stored group chunks for that URL are deleted and not replaced.

triageGrades.reason: crawlFilter.js:104 is the SKIP_SEGMENTS entry mapping /login and /register to a log rule name 'auth' — a string label, not authentication or authorization logic; the change touches no auth path.
No credentials, tokens or key handling anywhere in the diff; the only env addition is a log-level string.
No billing, Stripe, quota or pricing code is touched.
The diff adds no delete/overwrite operation — it only declines to enqueue URLs and declines to create chunks; the existing insert-before-delete path is unchanged.
No external API client or integration is modified; the crawl's HTTP/embedding calls are only indirectly reduced in number.
Only .env.example documentation is added and CRAWL_FILTER_LOG_LEVEL defaults to 'light', so no deploy, migration or version step is required.

summary: The local review found nothing and missed both real defects — including a high-severity silent drop of the LEO-018 hours chunk — and its single piece of triage evidence misreads a log-rule label as auth code.
